data.text/markdown:
overnight_open · does the night predict the first hour?

The question, before any trading: is there a direct connection between what happens after the close, overnight, in the pre-market and in the news, and a strong first trading hour the next day? And does that first hour follow the night's direction, or fade it? overnight_open_explore_marimo.py shows single nights, minute by minute. Data.
  • ~530 stocks with extended-hours 1-minute bars, 2025-06-18 → 2026-06-26. After that the database keeps extended hours for only 7 names.
  • The stocks were chosen as volatile, heavily traded names, with hindsight (the HighOctane list). So every number reads as "for volatile US stocks", and the market's own rise is always taken out.
  • SEC 8-K filings, timed to the second.
  • Benzinga headlines from 2025-10-14, dated but not timed.
What was found before. burst_scan's move_extended.ipynb (16 names, 2026-09-29):
  • The pre-market price IS the gap (r 0.999).
  • Extended hours barely improved the prediction of a big move near the open (AUC 0.687 → 0.700) and not its direction at all (0.544 → 0.539).
  • Evening moves clustered on news nights: "an earnings calendar is the missing input".
This notebook scales that to ~530 names and adds the news. Two windows. Discovery, July 2025 → February 2026: explore it freely; §1-§5 read only this window. Validation, March → June 2026: read ONCE in §6, with four questions whose pass bars were written into the README before anything was run.
  1. The night table and how much of it each source covers
  2. A strong first hour: twice the stock's usual first-hour range
  3. Size: which signals go with a strong first hour, and does each part of the night add to what the previous days already tell?
  4. Direction: does the first hour continue the night's move or fade it?
  5. Flags: unusual nights, compared with nights that moved just as much
  6. Validation: the four pre-registered questions on the months nobody looked at

1 · The night table

One row per stock and session: every signal known before 09:30 (research.FEATURES, in four groups: previous days, the night's price move, the night's trading activity, the news) and what the first hour did. Moves are in daily ATRs (the stock's typical daily range), so a 1-ATR night is equally big for a quiet and a wild stock; volumes are against the stock's own mean of the 20 sessions before. The first build takes about half an hour (cached after).
126,050 nights of 535 stocks: 82,617 in discovery (2025-07-08 → 2026-02-27), 43,433 in validation (locked until §6).

data.text/html: Table 1 · Coverage per month (share of nights). A stock without an after-hours or pre-market print that night has no value for those signals; a stock that never files 8-Ks (a foreign issuer, a fund) has none for the 8-K columns; headlines start on 2025-10-14.

data.text/markdown:
2 · A strong first hour

The first hour's high-low range (the official open included) divided by the stock's usual first-hour range: its median over the 20 sessions before. 1 = an ordinary first hour, 2 = twice as wide. A strong first hour reaches the threshold below. The pre-registered tests (§6) use 2, whatever the slider says.

data.text/markdown:
3 · Size: what goes with a strong first hour?

3a · Each signal alone. The rank correlation (IC) of every signal with the first hour's range relative to normal: +0.10 means nights ranked higher on the signal tend to have wider first hours. Moves enter as their size (a 2-ATR drop counts like a 2-ATR rise). Errors are clustered by day, because all stocks share one morning's market. One correlation is partly built in: fh_norm, the usual first-hour range, is the outcome's denominator. When it happens to read low, the same first hour counts as wider, so it leans negative by construction.

data.text/markdown: 3b · Dose-response. Nights sorted into ten equal groups by one signal: is the share of strong first hours higher where the signal is higher, and smoothly so? A real connection rises step by step; one group sticking out is more likely noise. Bars are ±2 standard errors clustered by day; the dashed line is the overall share.

data.text/markdown: 3c · The ladder: does each part of the night add? Four models, each with one more group of signals: the previous days alone, then the night's price move, then its trading activity, then the news. Every model is walked forward: each month is predicted by a model fit only on the months before it (a small gradient-boosted tree, fixed settings). The score is the AUC, the chance that a strong night is ranked above an ordinary one: 0.5 = a coin flip, 1 = perfect. A step's gain is its AUC minus the previous step's, with a 95% interval from resampling whole days. Scored on November 2025 → February 2026 (the headlines need a month to build their baseline); trained on everything before each month. This is the core answer to the question: if the night's move and activity add a clear gain over the previous days, the night is connected to the first hour's size. (Part of the previous days' own score is the built-in fh_norm effect of 3a, one more reason to read the gains, not the first bar.)
Click the button to run the ladder.

4 · Direction: does the first hour follow the night?

4a · Each signal alone, now with its sign: the IC of every signal with the first hour's return beyond the average stock that morning (the market taken out). A positive IC for the pre-market move means the first hour tends to continue the night; negative, to fade it.

data.text/markdown: 4b · Continue or fade, by kind of night. On nights whose pre-market moved at least 0.5 daily ATRs from the close: the first hour's return beyond the average stock, signed by the night's direction, in basis points (1 bp = 0.01%). Positive = it went on in the night's direction. For scale: a round trip in the first half hour costs roughly 20-40 bp for a $10k order (fade_movers' cost table), so a few bp is a connection, not a trade.

4c · The direction ladder. The same four walked-forward models as 3c, now predicting whether a stock's first hour beats the average stock that morning. 0.5 = no better than a coin flip. The earlier 16-name study found 0.54 at most, so expect little here.
Click the button to run the ladder.

5 · Flags: unusual nights

The flags of the explorer notebook, over all stocks. For each flag:
  • strong: the share of its nights with a strong first hour (§2's threshold);
  • strong if moved as much: the share among nights WITHOUT the flag whose pre-market moved just as far (same fifth of the move's size; no pre-market print is its own group);
  • lift: the difference, with its t clustered by day. A big lift says the flag tells something the move alone does not;
  • continuation: as in 4b, on the flag's moved nights.
The co-occurrence table shows how often one flag comes with another (row = given this flag, column = share that also has that one): earnings nights are usually busy, moving nights too.

data.text/html: Table 5a · The flags (discovery)Table 5b · Co-occurrence: share of the row flag's nights that also carry the column flagTable 5c · Hindsight only: headlines dated on the session day itself, which may have come out after the open, so never a signal. It shows how much a TIMED news feed could be worth: if same-day headlines go with far more strong first hours than the previous day's, the timing is what is missing.

data.text/markdown:
6 · Validation: the four pre-registered questions (read once)

Written into the README before anything ran. Each is scored on discovery (November 2025 → February 2026) and on the locked validation months (March → June 2026); the models are walked forward exactly as in §3c (trained on all months before the one scored), with a strong first hour fixed at 2× usual and a moved night at 0.5 ATR.
  • V1 · Does the night's price move add to the previous days, for a strong first hour? Passes when the AUC gain's 95% interval is above 0.
  • V2 · Do the night's trading activity and the news add beyond the move? Passes when the AUC gain's 95% interval is above 0.
  • V3 · Does the first hour continue (or fade) the night's move, beyond the market? Passes when |t| ≥ 2 with the same sign as in discovery.
  • V4 · Does it continue more (or less) on news nights than on quiet ones? Passes when |t| ≥ 2 with the same sign as in discovery.
Read it once: a second look after changing anything turns the validation months into discovery months. Turn the switch on, then click.
